scenario.topic: Decide how to redesign the office meeting-room booking policy

options.name: First-Come, First-Served Booking System
options.upside: Simple and transparent process encourages quick reservations.
options.concern: High demand may cause popular slots to fill quickly, limiting access.

options.name: Priority-Based Booking with Department Quotas
options.upside: Ensures fair room access across departments and seniority levels.
options.concern: Complexity may slow down booking and require administrative oversight.

options.name: Time-Block Allocation with Rotating Schedule
options.upside: Equitable distribution of meeting times reduces booking conflicts.
options.concern: Less flexibility for spontaneous meetings and urgent needs.

options.name: On-Demand Booking with Usage Tracking and Limits
options.upside: Encourages efficient room use and self-monitoring by users.
options.concern: Requires users to monitor their usage actively to avoid limits.

shared_context: The office meeting-room booking policy needs redesign to improve fairness and efficiency. Six participants will decide on a policy that balances booking flexibility, room utilization, and ease of use for all employees.

personas.name: Maya
personas.background: Maya manages a cross-functional team that requires regular collaboration across departments.
personas.private_goal: Ensure fair and predictable access to meeting rooms for all teams.

A.reason_for: Simple and transparent booking process is easy to understand.
A.reason_against: Popular slots fill quickly, which may frustrate teams needing regular access.

B.reason_for: Department quotas ensure fairness across teams and seniority.
B.reason_against: The complexity and administrative overhead might slow down the booking process.

C.reason_for: Equitable time-block rotation guarantees fair distribution and reduces conflicts.

D.reason_for: Real-time booking with usage tracking encourages efficient use of rooms.
D.reason_against: Users must actively monitor their usage, which could be a burden.

personas.name: Liam
personas.background: Liam is a senior engineer who values efficiency and quick access to resources.
personas.private_goal: Maximize flexibility and ease of booking to support fast-paced work.

A.reason_for: Quick, first-come booking fits well with spontaneous meeting needs.
A.reason_against: High demand may cause popular slots to be unavailable.

B.reason_for: Department quotas could provide some fairness.
B.reason_against: Complexity and priority rules slow down booking and add overhead.

C.reason_for: Fair rotation is good for long-term fairness.
C.reason_against: Rigid schedule limits flexibility needed for urgent meetings.

D.reason_for: On-demand booking with real-time availability supports fast, flexible use.

personas.name: Zoe
personas.background: Zoe is a junior analyst who often books rooms for small team check-ins.
personas.private_goal: Keep the booking process simple and accessible without complicated rules.

A.reason_for: Simple, transparent first-come system is easy to use and understand.

B.reason_against: Complexity and seniority priority make it harder to book simply.

C.reason_against: Less flexible for spontaneous meetings, which Zoe sometimes needs.

D.reason_for: Real-time booking and usage tracking encourage efficient use.
D.reason_against: Monitoring usage actively may be a hassle.

personas.name: Eli
personas.background: Eli is a department head who frequently schedules large meetings and presentations.
personas.private_goal: Ensure reliable access to rooms for important meetings without delays.

A.reason_for: First-come system is straightforward and fast for booking important meetings.

B.reason_for: Priority and quotas help secure rooms for senior staff like Eli.
B.reason_against: Booking complexity could slow down the process.

C.reason_against: Rigid rotation limits ability to book urgent large meetings.

D.reason_against: Shorter max duration and usage limits may restrict longer meetings.

personas.name: Nina
personas.background: Nina is a project coordinator who organizes frequent quick check-ins and brainstorming sessions.
personas.private_goal: Maximize booking flexibility with easy access to rooms for short meetings.

A.reason_for: Simple first-come booking is easy and fast for quick meetings.
A.reason_against: Popular slots may be unavailable during peak times.

B.reason_against: Complexity and priority rules add friction to booking.

D.reason_for: On-demand mobile booking with usage limits supports efficient, flexible use.

personas.name: Omar
personas.background: Omar is a senior manager who values structured fairness and clear priority rules.
personas.private_goal: Ensure senior staff and departments have fair and prioritized access to rooms.

A.reason_for: Simple booking is easy to understand.
A.reason_against: First-come system does not guarantee fairness or priority for senior staff.

B.reason_for: Priority-based quotas ensure fairness and respect seniority, aligning with Omar’s values.

C.reason_for: Rotating schedule fairly distributes room time among teams.

D.reason_against: Limits and self-monitoring may be inconvenient.

Real-time booking and usage tracking encourage efficient use.
